newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Accor Asia Pacific targets New Zealand hotels.
newsitem.headline: Accor Asia Pacific targets New Zealand hotels.

text.p: Asia Pacific's largest hotel group, Accor Asia Pacific (AAPC Ltd), said on Wednesday it was making a major expansion in New Zealand with the addition of three hotels.
AAPC, which already has Novotel hotels in Auckland and Rotorua, has bought the Terrace Regency Hotel in Wellington and the former Holiday Inn Queenstown.
It has also signed an agreement to manage an all-suites hotel currently under construction in Queenstown and due for completion in early 1998.
Accor Asia Pacific said it was the largest hotel group in Asia Pacific, with 127 hotels and over 24,000 rooms in 115 countries. The company's brands are Sofitel, Novotel, Mercure and Ibis.
The Wellington hotel, with 108 rooms, will undergo and extensive renovation programme, and will be renamed the Novotel Wellington in July.

The 150-room Holiday Inn Queenstown will be rebranded the Novotel Queenstown from February 12. It has been purchased by Tourism Asset Holdings Ltd, an affiliate of AAPC Ltd, and will be managed by Accor Asia Pacific.

The other Queenstown hotel, currently being built, will be called the Novotel Suites Queenstown. It will be an apartment-style hotel with 83 apartments ranging from studios to two level penthouses, with full hotel service.

The new hotels announced following the signing in 1996 of an agreement for the development of the Novotel Hamilton, with construction due to begin in March and completion expected toward the end of 1998.
AAPC's first hotel in New Zealand, the Novotel Auckland, is set to complete a multi-million dollar upgrading programme.
AAPC's chief executive of Australian and New Zealand operations, Michael Issenberg, said the company was very confident about the potential of the New Zealand market.
He said the economy was growing strongly and inbound tourism was in a healthy state.
